source.title: Theory IIIb: Generalization in Deep Networks
source.authors: T. Poggio; Q. Liao; B. Miranda; Andrzej Banburski; X. Boix; J. Hidary

record.tranche_reason: Tests how training-set size, parameter count, and weight perturbations relate to training and test error using its own experiments; its CIFAR experiments are conceptually related but do not reproduce the versions' named settings and measures.
record.gate_note: Figure 1 reports error across training-set sizes for natural and random labels. Figure 2 reports classification error and cross-entropy risk across parameter counts. Figure 5 reports training and test error under repeated weight perturbations. No results are extracted from cited prior work.
record.test_reason: The paper reports its own random-label fitting and natural-label generalization experiments relevant to V1, and a width sweep relevant to V2, in a five-layer CIFAR-10 convolutional network. The supplied text establishes random-label interpolation and non-increasing classification error with width, but does not establish all parts of either version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors claim that gradient-flow dynamics near zero-loss solutions provide local minimum-norm or maximum-margin behavior for exponential-type losses, explaining why classification error often does not worsen with overparameterization on low-noise data. They explicitly distinguish this explanation from explaining why test error is low, and allow some overfitting in expected loss.
record.recipe_differences: Uses gradient descent on CIFAR-10 with cross-entropy and no data augmentation or explicit regularization; the random-label experiment uses SGD, batch size 100, and 70 epochs. The paper also reports a gradient-descent weight-perturbation experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset size and parameter count are varied; in Figure 5, repeated weight perturbations change expected risk while training error returns to zero.

fits_no_version.finding: Repeated weight perturbations followed by gradient descent restore empirical risk while expected risk increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Repeated perturbation and retraining can worsen held-out risk despite recovery of training fit.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing network width produces small cross-entropy-risk overfitting without a reported increase in classification error.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Held-out cross-entropy and classification error can respond differently to increasing network width.

record.problems: The width-sweep and training-set-size results are largely presented in figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The text does not state chance-level held-out performance for random labels. The theory concerns gradient flow near zero minima; the paper notes that its experimental simulations use GD or, in one setup, SGD.

untested.parts: The named Inception, AlexNet, MLP, and ImageNet settings are not tested.
The specified one-hidden-layer networks and MNIST/downsampled-CIFAR-10 settings are not tested; convergence and the interpolation threshold are not established.
No convolutional-versus-fully-connected training comparison or learned-local-connectivity experiment.
No batch-size comparison under controlled training budgets.
No ranking of generalization gaps by magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance or comparison with competing measures.
No removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source listed for these versions. No V2 verdict is justified by the available wording: non-increase does not imply a plateau or continued decrease. Missing chance comparisons for V1 are reporting limitations, not evidence against the claim. The figures themselves are not visually available in the supplied text.

versions.untested_parts: The text does not state held-out accuracy relative to chance for random labels, and does not report the specified small Inception, AlexNet, MLP, or ImageNet settings.
Tests a five-layer convolutional CIFAR-10 network, not one-hidden-layer ReLU networks on MNIST or downsampled CIFAR-10; reports no test-error decrease beyond the interpolation threshold.

rows.subject: 5-layer convolutional network with 16 channels per hidden layer
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of training examples using natural CIFAR-10 labels; trained by minimizing cross-entropy.
rows.measure: Training and generalization error across training-set sizes
rows.note: The figure provides the plotted values; no numerical values are stated in the text.
rows.check: Section 2 explicitly reports decreasing test error with more natural-label examples, including where training error is zero. However, the supplied figure text does not establish held-out accuracy far above chance, as V1 requires.

rows.subject: 5-layer convolutional network with 16 channels per hidden layer
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number of training examples using random CIFAR-10 labels; trained by minimizing cross-entropy.
rows.measure: Training and generalization error across training-set sizes
rows.note: The authors state that Figure 1 suggests generalization for increasing training-set size with random labels, but do not state held-out accuracy relative to chance.
rows.check: Section 2 explicitly establishes zero training error on randomly labeled data, so the memorization component is readable from the text. Chance-level held-out accuracy remains undetermined. The authors' convergence of training and expected errors does not mean successful prediction of random held-out labels.

rows.subject: DNN; architecture not stated in the Figure 2 discussion
rows.size_stated: number of parameters varied; exact values not stated
rows.operation_detail: Increased the number of parameters without changing the multilayer architecture.
rows.value: does not get worse when the number of parameters increases well beyond the size of the training set
rows.note: The authors explicitly describe the trend; numerical error values are only plotted.
rows.check: Parameter-count robustness does not measure V1's natural-versus-random-label comparison. This duplicates R4 and should be merged with it. Figure 2 identifies the architecture as the same five-layer convolutional network as Figure 1. Non-increasing error does not establish continued decreasing error beyond interpolation.

rows.subject: DNN; architecture not stated in the Figure 2 discussion
rows.size_stated: number of parameters varied; exact values not stated
rows.operation_detail: Increased the number of parameters without changing the multilayer architecture.
rows.value: does not show an increase when the number of neurons is increased
rows.note: This reports no increase rather than the version's predicted continued lowering of test error; the experiment is a five-layer convolutional CIFAR-10 network, not the specified shallow-network settings.
rows.check: The reported absence of an increase neither establishes nor rules out continued lowering of test error. Marking the effect absent is unsupported. The text also does not locate the zero-training-error width threshold or establish training to convergence.

rows.subject: DNN; architecture not stated in the Figure 2 discussion
rows.size_stated: number of parameters varied; exact values not stated
rows.operation_detail: Increased the number of parameters without changing the multilayer architecture.
rows.note: The authors say the peculiarities of the exponential loss exaggerate the overfitting.
rows.check: Cross-entropy risk is a different measure from V2's test classification error. Small risk overfitting is explicitly reported, but it cannot determine any listed version's effect. Figure 2 identifies the network as the Figure 1 architecture.

rows.subject: 5-layer convolutional neural network; 4 convolutional layers and a fully connected layer
rows.size_stated: hidden-layer channels 16, 32, 64 and 128; parameter count not stated
rows.stage_stated: trained with GD; perturbations began after roughly 1800 epochs at zero training classification error
rows.operation_detail: Added Gaussian noise to every layer after every 100 training epochs, then continued gradient descent.

conditions.value: Gaussian noise with standard deviation being 1/4 of that of the weights of the corresponding layer

rows.measure: Classification error on training and test data
rows.value: Training classification error returns to zero; expected risk grows increasingly higher during perturbations
rows.note: The caption describes the result; precise plotted errors are figure-only. This perturbation result is not named by a claim version.
rows.check: Repeated perturbations followed by retraining do not measure V7's association between perturbation tolerance and generalization gaps across networks. Separate classification error from cross-entropy risk: the caption explicitly describes increasing expected risk, while precise classification-error outcomes require the plot.

rows.subject: 5-layer convolutional neural network; 4 convolutional layers and a fully connected layer
rows.size_stated: hidden-layer channels 16, 32, 64 and 128; parameter count not stated
rows.operation_detail: Measured classification error, cross-entropy risk, and weight norms during training as a no-perturbation control.
rows.measure: Classification error, cross-entropy risk, and L2 norm of weights
rows.note: The caption identifies this as the control experiment but gives no numerical outcomes.
rows.check: The control does not test a listed version. Split classification error, cross-entropy risk, and weight norms into separate measures if retained; their numerical outcomes cannot be recovered from the supplied plot text.

relationships.condition: Random-label memorization component in the five-layer CIFAR-10 convolutional network
relationships.reason: Section 2 explicitly states that the network achieves zero training error on random labels (R2); this supports the capacity component, while the full held-out comparison remains unresolved.
relationships.display_finding: The reported zero random-label training error remains unverified from the available source, and the paired held-out comparison is unresolved.
